speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient has hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She also has a history of high cholesterol. Social history: Retired school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Glioblastoma Multiforme. The combination of a 69-year-old woman presenting with a progressive headache and worsening vision over three weeks, alongside a history of hypertension, is highly suggestive of a high-grade glioma causing increased intracranial pressure and optic nerve compression. The absence of systemic symptoms and the specific progression pattern point away from infectious or inflammatory etiologies. Further neuro-ophthalmologic evaluation and neurosurgical consultation are urgently indicated.
